local_articles.title: Jeff Bezos-backed group nears Liverpool deal as billionaire consortium closes in on significant stake: Report
local_articles.snippet: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is reportedly part of an investor consortium closing in on a deal to acquire a significant minority stake in Liverpool, with the transaction potentially set to be announced within days. The consortium, led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, is expected to acquire more than 30 per cent of the Premier League champions from owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG). Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is also understood to be part of the investor group. According to Sky News, which first reported the latest development, FSG is preparing for a possible announcement as early as this week, although the completion of the transaction could slip into next week. The proposed investment is expected to value Liverpool at around $6 billion, representing a remarkable increase from the £300 million FSG paid to acquire the club in 2010. questions.title: Who will be appointed to succeed Pape Thiaw as head coach of Senegal's men's national football team by August 31, 2026?
questions.background: The Senegalese Football Federation is responsible for appointing the national team's head coach.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the Senegalese Football Federation, as confirmed by contemporaneous reliable news reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the person publicly announced as Pape Thiaw's successor between August 1 and August 31, 2026. The resolution date is the date the appointment is publicly announced, rather than the coach's presentation or first match. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-15 breaking news across four outlets and two independent sourcing lines naming Patrick Vieira as Pape Thiaw's chosen successor (SeneNews Aug 15 08:23 & 14:15, Pan Africa Football exclusive Aug 15, Seneweb Aug 15 16:01/22:13, Blueprint Aug 15): SeneNews and Seneweb (citing Sports News Africa's Malang Sane) report Vieira has reached agreement on a four-year 'Vision 2030' contract with the FSF paying 35-45M FCFA/month (targets: AFCON 2027 final, WC 2030 qualification). Independently, Pan Africa Football cites an FSF federation source confirming the federation has selected Vieira, with official announcement expected next week after final formalities, and adds that Malick Daf (Teungueth FC) is among three finalists to serve as Vieira's assistant coach (effectively removing Malick Daf as head-coach contender). Because the FSF has not yet issued the official public announcement—retaining ~25% residual risk of a late Ministry of Sports salary/budget snag, final-formality collapse, or premature scoop—we lift Patrick Vieira sharply from 0.55 -> 0.75 (well below our 0.85 unannounced cap) while keeping shortlist backups Omar Daf (0.18 -> 0.08), Habib Beye (0.08 -> 0.05), Souleymane Diallo (0.05 -> 0.03), and Malick Daf (0.03 -> 0.01; sum = 0.92, 8% residual).

local_articles.title: Novak Djokovic ousted from Cincinnati Open in his first match since Wimbledon
local_articles.snippet: MASON, Ohio: Novak Djokovic’s stay at the Cincinnati Open was a short one. The 24-time major champion fell to Thiago Agustin Tirante 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 on Saturday in a match that took 2 hours, 44 minutes in hot and humid conditions. A 25-year-old from Argentina, Tirante is ranked No. 50 in the world. The 39-year-old Djokovic — a three-time Cincinnati Open champion and No. 5 in the rankings — was playing for the first time since his loss to top-ranked Jannik Sinner in the semifinals at Wimbledon. Up next for Djokovic is the US Open, which starts Aug. 30. Djokovic appeared to struggle physically in the heat and had his 10-match winning streak in Cincinnati snapped. He won the title in 2020 and 2023. Djokovic saved 13 of the 15 break points he faced. questions.title: Who will be the first major Ukrainian political figure to publicly call for wartime elections following Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion?
questions.background: Ukrainian law bars elections during wartime. The presidential election has been postponed under continuing martial law, although Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s presidential term ended in May 2024.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Qualifying Event : Identify the person credited in reliable reporting with the first public call by a major Ukrainian political figure since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion to resume national elections while the war continues. A call solely for elections after the war ends does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the qualifying statement becomes public, provided this occurs by August 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The politician’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-12 refresh (first update since June 24) incorporating July-August Ukrainian political upheaval: (1) Volodymyr Zelenskyy rises to #1 (0.16 -> 0.21) after Ukrainska Pravda (July) and NV.ua (Aug 8) reported Zelenskyy privately told Ambassador Valerii Zaluzhnyi in Kyiv that 'most likely we will have to hold elections this autumn' citing a frontline window and social consolidation, before publicly denying plans on July 2 and launching a sweeping mid-July cabinet reshuffle ('changing its political strategy'). (2) Valerii Zaluzhnyi surges (0.10 -> 0.16): confirmed privately to Zelenskyy he would run in autumn elections, broke public political orthodoxy on Aug 3 declaring Ukraine will 'never actually join' NATO (Reuters/Evropeiska Pravda), and crushes Zelenskyy 47.4% to 24.2% in a runoff in today's Aug 12 Socis poll (fielded July 28-Aug 2, n=2,000, MrEast.eu). (3) Mykhailo Fedorov enters at #4 (0.00 -> 0.13): ousted by Zelenskyy as Defense Minister on July 15 sparking downtown Kyiv protests and military resignations, now freed from cabinet discipline with strong Washington ties and surging to 3rd in the first round (10.5%) and a 43.4%-24.7% runoff rout of Zelenskyy in today's Socis poll. (4) Petro Poroshenko trims (0.22 -> 0.16): still leader of the largest parliamentary opposition party (European Solidarity) with strong anti-Zelenskyy incentives, though polling just 4.9% in the Aug 12 Socis survey and trailing Zelenskyy 20.7%-38.1% in a runoff. (5) Vitali Klitschko trims (0.18 -> 0.11) as a vocal Western-media critic of Zelenskyy's centralization, while Yulia Tymoshenko drops from the top 5 (absent from the Aug 12 Socis leaders and 2026 election coverage) into the 23% residual alongside Tymoshenko, Kyrylo Budanov, Dmytro Razumkov, Yulia Svyrydenko, and Ruslan Stefanchuk. OPORA (July 10) confirms martial law still bars elections and no bill is registered.

questions.title: To which hospital will Pakistan’s Supreme Court order Imran Khan transferred for medical care in August 2026?
questions.background: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan is imprisoned at Adiala jail. His eye condition has required specialist treatment, and concerns about his health have been central to his party’s campaign for his release.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Supreme Court’s order or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations describing its requirements. Resolution : Resolve to the hospital designated in the Supreme Court’s next order, issued after the start date and during August 2026, directing Khan’s transfer from Adiala jail for hospital care. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the hospital.

Fixing the hearing before an independent, fundamental-rights-oriented three-judge bench amid a confirmed two-month lapse in eye care strengthens the odds that an August 18 transfer order grants the petitioners' explicitly prayed venue — lifting Shifa International Hospital +0.04 (0.44 -> 0.48) while keeping strong calibrated mass on federal default Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (0.26 -> 0.24) and neutral eye-specialty compromise Al-Shifa Trust Eye Hospital (0.21 -> 0.19, where Adiala authorities took Bushra Bibi on July 28). Armed Forces Institute of Ophthalmology (0.03) and Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital (0.02) hold steady (sum = 0.96, 4% residual).

local_articles.title: The case of former Pakistan PM Imran Khan: US amnesia on democracy
local_articles.snippet: Three years after his arrest, Pakistan’s former Prime Minister Imran Khan remains incarcerated, with no definitive indication that his release is imminent. Although recent speculation has centred on the possibility of a medical release, these discussions remain contingent on broader political calculations rather than legal momentum. At 73, Khan continues to be held primarily in solitary confinement at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, serving sentences in multiple cases, including the Toshakhana and Al-Qadir Trust convictions, which both he and the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) insist are politically engineered by Pakistan’s military establishment in concert with the Shehbaz Sharif government. Khan continues to face dozens of additional legal proceedings, ensuring that even favourable outcomes in individual cases would not necessarily secure his freedom. local_articles.title: Supreme Court Fight Erupts Over Plot to End MAGA’s Grip
local_articles.snippet: Democratic lawmakers are taking aim at the Supreme Court to curb its rightward shift. They’ve grown increasingly frustrated by the court, as it has delivered sweeping conservative victories in recent years, erasing decades of progress, including scaling back the 1965 Voting Rights Act, overturning the constitutional right to an abortion, loosening campaign finance rules, and increasing executive power. Some in the party have argued that recent rulings from the high court are more about politics, and less about the interpretation of the law. “And I think the continuing interest in reform springs from continued dismay and concern about the court’s misbehavior,” he added. In response, Democratic lawmakers have introduced several bills in recent months aimed at curbing the Supreme Court amid its rightward shift.
